“The rat said,
‘Friends are of two kinds: one of them is the sincere friend, and the other is the one who creates bonds of brotherhood with someone
while in a state of compulsion. The sincere friend must prefer.
his friend over himself, his possessions, and his kin.

As for the friend who is compelled into amity,
it could happen that both the enmity and the amity become fulfilled; but oftentimes, they disband, going unfulfilled
and stale.

But a wise man should watch out for himself. his truce is like him who eats
For he who reconciles with the enemy, trusts him, acts in his interest, and does not watch out for himself-

p.n: Trusting a Foe Is Like Eating Bad Food

body.p:
his truce
is that of he who eats the food which fulfills his fancy, and whose stomach cannot digest.

p.n: The Rat Acknowledges His Remaining Obligation

body.p: I have finished my work, and some is due still;
but every action has a set time at which it should be carried out,
and whoever doesn’t carry out a work at its set time, does not reap the fruits of his work.

p.n: The Rat Explains Not Cutting the Last Rope

body.p:
‘I will cut your bonds, leaving one cord, which I will take as a security, for you to cut yourself, so that you could not
catch me, when you become free from your bonds.’
“When morning came, and the huntsman arrived at the place,

p.n: The Cat Breaks from the Last Rope

body.p: and pulled at the cord, not expecting it to be cut, but the cord did,

p.n: The Cat and the Rat Escape

body.p: and both survived The cat climbed the tree, the rat went into the burrow, and the huntsman left
